attention4.ptxt: The vacuum pump will lose its original performance if it is disassembled.
Do not disassemble and repair the vacuum pump. If any faulty condition is found, replace the vacuum pump with a new one.

s1.ptxt: Disconnect negative (–) cable at battery.
Remove engine cover.
Drain coolant.
Remove air cleaner suction pipe No.2 (1).
Disconnect connector from boost pressure sensor with IAT sensor-2 (2).
Remove intercooler outlet pipe No.2 (3).
Disconnect vacuum hose (1) and waste gate control hose No.2 (2) from vacuum pump.
Remove thermostat cap bolt (3) and nut (4), and intercooler outlet pipe No.2 bracket (5).
Tighten thermostat cap bolt (1) and nut (2) securely, and cover thermostat cap with shop cloth (3).

attention4.ptxt: If leaking oil from camshaft end adheres to thermostat, thermostat rubber ring could be damaged and cause coolant leakage.
To prevent oil from adhering to thermostat, tighten thermostat cap bolt and nut and cover thermostat cap with shop cloth.

s1.ptxt: Remove vacuum pump (4) with O-ring.
Clean mating surfaces of thermostat case and vacuum pump.
Install new O-ring (1) to vacuum pump.
Install vacuum pump (2) to thermostat case (3) aligning vacuum pump coupling (4) with slit (5) of camshaft.
Tighten vacuum pump bolts (1) to specified torque.
Remove thermostat cap bolt (2) and nut (3).
Install intercooler outlet pipe No.2 bracket and tighten thermostat cap bolt and nut to specified torque.
Connect waste gate control hose No.2 (1) and vacuum hose (2).
Install intercooler outlet pipe No.2 (1), and fix radiator inlet hose (2) and outlet hose (3) with clamps on intercooler outlet pipe No.2.
Tighten intercooler outlet pipe No.2 clamps to specified torque.
Connect boost pressure sensor with IAT sensor-2 (1) connector.
Install air cleaner suction pipe No.2 (2).
Refill cooling system with coolant.
Check cooling system for leakage.
Install engine cover.
Connect negative (–) cable at battery.
